You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The most likely match is late 2024 or early 2025.

The 10-year yield rose sharply over 3 months and 12 months, which fits a period like Dec 2024 or Jan 2025. At that point the Fed had cut but the long end sold off. The 10y-2y spread is very high relative to the prior 36 months, since it was deeply inverted in 2022-2023. VIX is low against a year earlier, and the Baa spread is tight. The dollar is at -2.5, which looks odd for late 2024, when the dollar was strong.

A weak dollar with a high spread and a rising 10-year yield could also fit late 2025 or early 2026, but the 10-year did not rise 2 SD over 3 months then. Core CPI at -2.0 suggests low core inflation relative to the past 3 years, which were high at the start of the window. That points to a time when the 36-month window includes the 2022-2023 inflation peak, so 2025 or later.

An alternative is 2013 (the taper tantrum), when the 10-year rose sharply, bonds sold off, and gold fell. But the stock-bond correlation was not positive then, and the policy rate would sit near zero. The policy rate at -1.5 against a 36-month window rather than a zero-bound period suggests 2021 instead. Early 2021 fits: the 10-year rose sharply over 3 months, the 10y-2y spread widened, bonds sold off, gold fell, equity 12m returns were strong, the Baa spread was tight, and the dollar was weak. The policy rate of -1.5 would reflect the window including 2018-2019 rates, and the dollar at -2.5 over 12 months fits the 2020-21 fall. Headline CPI 3m change of +1.0 fits early 2021. Core CPI at -2.0 fits as well, because it was low in 2021 versus the 2018-2020 window. The correlation being positive at +3 is less certain for early 2021, but plausible. The 12m VIX change of -3.0 fits March 2020 versus March 2021, and the Baa spread 12m change of -3.0 does too.

Industrial production at -0.5 and unemployment +0.5 are consistent. The best month is March 2021, when the 10-year yield rose sharply and the 3m bond return was most negative.
